Lorcan Vane.narrative: I'm a Vane of Low Row, and I fish the Fish Steps at first light like my father did before the fever took him. The mornings are honest; it's the nights that cost me. Under the arcade, with the counters warm in my hand, I can feel a run coming — and then Roos or old Aldous takes it off me and I owe a little more. I mean to win it all back one night. Davin doesn't say much about it, which is worse than if he shouted.
goals: Win back everything I owe in one good night at counters
Pay off the nine drops written in Aldous Quill's ledger
Settle with Dolly at the Marver before she stops serving me
See Wick grow up knowing his father's brothers
pastimes: Counters under the arcade every night
Sitting on the quay edge mending a line at dusk
A mug at the Marver with Eamon Tarn
Lorcan Vane.calling: Line fishing at first light is the work I was made for; I'd be content if the nights didn't undo it.

relations.name: Davin Vane
relations.label: brother
relations.note: Steady as a stone, and he never once scolds me for the counters. I'd do the same for him.

relations.name: Petra Tarn
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She runs the smokehouse and a house of five and still asks after me. She got the better of the three of us.

relations.name: Wick Marl
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: Sander's boy. I owe it to Sander to be something Wick can look at.

relations.name: Thessaly Marl
relations.label: Wick's mother
relations.note: Night watch at the Cone, and she never asks me for a drop. I respect that more than I say.

relations.name: Aldous Quill
relations.label: tally keeper
relations.note: He writes my losses neat as a grave marker and never loses himself. Nine drops, in his book, in his hand.

relations.name: Roos Achterberg
relations.label: counters rival
relations.note: She takes my drops most nights and smiles doing it. One night the board will turn.

relations.name: Dolly Achterberg
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: Good cook, sharp eye. She's kept my tab open longer than she should have.

relations.name: Chidi Okoro
relations.label: line-maker
relations.note: Best line on the island and he knows it. I owe him for the last spool and he hasn't pressed me.

relations.name: Eamon Tarn
relations.label: drinking friend
relations.note: My sister's good-brother. We put the town to rights at the Marver most evenings.

relations.name: Neve Calloway
relations.label: fellow fisher
relations.note: Fishes beside me at the Steps and outs me every time. Sharp tongue, good hand.

relations.name: Magda Tarn
relations.label: catch divider
relations.note: She divides fair, even to a Vane who owes everybody. I'd not cross her.

relations.name: Rafe Dunlin
relations.label: night fisher
relations.note: Fishes the mole by the lamp while I'm losing at counters. Sensible man.

memories.gist: The fever winter: Sander went out to the mole in the cold and never came back, and Wick was born the next winter without him.
The night I won four drops straight off Roos and felt like the best player in Cullet — then gave them all back before the arcade emptied.
Aldous Quill reading my name out of the ledger in front of the arches, and the nine drops going in the book in his neat hand.
Last autumn's storm took the end rail of the mole; I helped Davin and the others haul the broken timber up before the sea got it.
A morning at the Fish Steps when the fish came so thick Magda gave me a double share, and I carried half of it to Petra's smokehouse.
Davin pushing the handcart up the wynd with a load of peat, and me thinking he works harder than any of us and gets no notice for it.

stances.why: Every loss is just the board waiting to turn; I've felt the run coming.
Sander's gone and Wick's here; whatever I owe, the Vanes stand together.
The book is open to anyone who asks, and my name's in it in Aldous's hand.
Whatever the night takes, the morning catch is clean and mine.
He's never once mentioned my debts and I'd rather not hear him start.

Davin Vane.narrative: I push the handcart and walk the Heron's wheel, and the town pays me a drop here and there for it. It's not a trade, whatever anyone says — a man wants something he can hand down. Lorcan's my brother and he's drowning in drops a little at a time, so I've been paying a bit of it off quiet, through Dolly, with Aldous writing it. He mustn't know. He'd take it as pity, and it isn't that.
values: a trade to call my own
goals: Find work that is mine, not just carrying for others
Clear the rest of Lorcan's Marver debt without him finding out
Save enough drops to set up properly one day
Keep Wick and Petra from ever needing to worry about the brothers
pastimes: Walking the strand at low tide looking at what the sea's left
A quiet mug at the Marver after the cart's put away
Riding Wick on the handcart when the load's light
Davin Vane.calling: I'd be a boatwright or a smith if the island had room for another — something where the work stays made after the day's done.

relations.name: Lorcan Vane
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He'd give me his last drop if I asked, which is exactly why he's in the book and I'm not.

relations.name: Petra Tarn
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She's got a head for the smokehouse and a heart for all of us. I'd tell her anything but this.

relations.name: Wick Marl
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: Sander's boy. When I put him on the cart he laughs the whole length of Low Row.

relations.name: Dolly Achterberg
relations.label: keeper of my secret
relations.note: She took the six drops without a word and put it against Lorcan's tab. She's never breathed it.

relations.name: Aldous Quill
relations.label: tally keeper
relations.note: He wrote it in the book as I asked and said nothing more. A careful man.

relations.name: Thessaly Marl
relations.label: Wick's mother
relations.note: She works the night watch and trusts me with her boy's name. I'd not let her down.

relations.name: Bram Calloway
relations.label: the boatwright
relations.note: I walk his wheel when he lifts a load. He builds a ship and I carry for it; I'd like to build something.

relations.name: Tam Roon
relations.label: peat man
relations.note: I cart his peat down and he pays fair. He grumbles about the Cone's price and I listen.

relations.name: Nan Fenwick
relations.label: customer
relations.note: She pays me to cart kelp up the wynds and always wants more than the gatherers bring.

relations.name: Eamon Tarn
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He drinks with Lorcan at the Marver. I keep my mouth shut and drink with them.

relations.name: Kit Calloway
relations.label: young friend
relations.note: A boy who wants to be something. I know how that feels and I've told him so.

memories.gist: The fever winter: Sander drowned off the mole in the cold, and I carried his body up with Lorcan and could not speak.
Dolly counting six drops into her palm at the Marver's back door and saying she'd put it on Lorcan's tab and tell no one.
Aldous Quill writing the six drops in the ledger in his neat hand and asking me once, only once, if I was sure.
Walking the Heron's wheel all afternoon while Bram lifted the new frame timber into the dry dock, and my legs shaking after.
The storm last autumn took slates off Low Row and I spent two days hauling them down to Gwil Stannard's cart.
Putting Wick on the empty handcart and running him along the quay, and him shouting for more.

stances.why: If Lorcan knew, he'd never take another drop from me, and he'd sink.
Anyone with a back can push a cart; I want work that leaves something standing.
The whole town talks at the wash-house wall and I'd rather not be talked about.
Aldous keeps it straight; better a written debt than a remembered one.
Kit and Wick will need someone to tell them the truth and not laugh at them.

Davin Vane.secret: I have paid six drops of Lorcan's debt to the Marver without telling him. Dolly knows, and Aldous wrote it.
